title: Statues, Macaws, and the Merlion at Midnight
excerpt: A thunderstorm at River Wonders, a stubborn scavenger hunt for newly unveiled statues in Fort Canning Park, and ending the night face-to-face with Singapore's most iconic symbol — all in one very full day.

photos.alt: Two bronze sculptural figures of Stamford Raffles and Nathaniel Wallich lit by ground spotlights in a lush nighttime garden at Fort Canning Park
Ya Kun Traditional Breakfast set on a red tray: soft-boiled eggs, kaya toast, iced black coffee, and a small glass of condensed milk
A large manatee gliding just below the surface of vivid green water, surrounded by floating aquatic plants at River Wonders
A young woman walks past the green Haji Lane street sign and a one-way arrow beside shophouse boutiques on a narrow Singapore street
A hand holding a small red-and-white Marigold HL high-calcium low-fat milk carton
Fort Canning Centre, a white colonial-era building with a red-tiled roof, seen across a wide manicured lawn under an overcast sky
Interior of a Godiva chocolate café counter with backlit menu boards and a large 'Godiva is Chocolate' advertising banner on the wall
The Esplanade Theatres by the Bay at night, its spiky durian-shaped dome glowing under a dramatic dark sky with a lone figure walking below
A traveler in a white NASA shirt leans against the red-painted iron railing of Cavenagh Bridge over Singapore River at night
A young man poses in front of the illuminated Merlion statue at Merlion Park, playfully tilting his head back as if catching the water jet in his mouth, Singapore's city skyline visible behind
